title: Introduce eventstream fragment stabilizer and toolcall lease sanitizer
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Stabilizes the eventstream (SSE) path by adding a Fragment Stabilizer that deterministically reassembles split/partial JSON frames and a Toolcall Lease Sanitizer to prevent overlapping tool/function call handoffs. Motivation: We continue to see user-facing incidents where mid-JSON SSE fragments or interleaved toolcall events yielded invalid or out-of-order structured outputs (partial JSON, duplicate delimiters, and token boundary loss). This PR provides conservative, well-tested guards that reduce incorrect partial emits and make toolcall handoffs idempotent under retries.
detailed_changes: What changed: 1) eventstream/fragment_stabilizer: New module that tracks fragment epochs and uses a small per-stream ledger (epoch anchor + 16-bit rolling checksum) to validate reassembly windows. The stabilizer enforces a deterministic coalescing policy: accept in-order fragments up to N windows, emit a resync marker when detection fails, and provide a probe-based resumption handshake. 2) toolcall/lease_sanitizer: Introduces a lease token for tool/function handoffs. When a toolcall sentinel is emitted, the lease provides a short-lived ownership window. Late-arriving fragments that would otherwise re-trigger the same toolcall are mapped through the lease table and deduplicated or converted to resume messages. 3) delimiter_normalizer: Normalizes commonly-observed delimiter patterns (duplicate newlines, trimmed trailing commas) before parsing structured JSON in the streaming path. 4) Backpressure adjustments: The stabilizer integrates with the existing backpressure controller to permit small windowed buffering (configurable via streaming.fragment_buffer_ms) to reduce false-positive resyncs. 5) Tests & docs: Adds deterministic integration tests (simulated network reorders and partial emits), unit coverage for lease expiry, and updated API docs describing streaming resync semantics.

review_comments: Evan Liu: Can we make the stabilizer window configurable per-customer? Response: added streaming.fragment_buffer_ms (default 40ms) and a feature gate for Dedicated customers in config; documented in streaming_resync.md.
Priya Nair: Concern about lease table growth under high-cardinality streams. Response: implemented bounded LRU with TTL eviction and metrics; added unit test verifying bounded growth.
Samir Khan: Suggest using CRC16 rather than ad-hoc checksum. Response: switched to a lightweight CRC16 implementation and measured no measurable perf regression in microbenchmarks.
Evan Liu: Approve after addressing lease eviction and adding integration test. Priya Nair: Approve.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: This change is backward-compatible for existing streaming clients. The stabilizer emits explicit resync markers ("<redwood:resync>") which are ignored by older clients — documented behavior. The lease sanitizer only affects server-side handoff semantics and does not change client-visible toolcall payloads unless a dedupe/convert to resume is required. No configuration migration required for hosted users; Dedicated customers can tune fragment_buffer_ms.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout: 1) Enable default stabilizer in Canary control plane for 5% of traffic (2 clusters) with extra logging, 2) monitor stream_reassembly_error_rate and toolcall_retries via dashboard, 3) after 48h and stable metrics, expand to 50% then 100%. For Dedicated/private installs, this will be included in upcoming release notes and can be toggled via config.
observability_changes: Added metrics: stream_reassembly_attempts, stream_resync_emits, toolcall_lease_conflicts, lease_evictions. Added a per-stream tag to reassembly metrics for easier triage. Dashboards and alerts: Stream Reassembly Error Rate (P2 alert), Toolcall Lease Conflict Spike (P3).
performance_notes: Microbenchmarks: stabilizer + CRC16 check adds ~0.4us per fragment in hot path and reduces unnecessary resyncs by 78% in our synthetic reorder test. Memory: lease table default bounded to 1024 entries per runtime instance; measured resident increase <1.2MB under synthetic load.
release_notes: Improve streaming (SSE) stability by deterministically reassembling partial JSON frames and preventing duplicate/overlapping tool/function call handoffs. Adds opt-in tuning knobs for fragment buffering and lease TTL. Backwards compatible; default behaviour enabled.
manual_steps: When deploying to on-prem: ensure config streaming.fragment_buffer_ms and toolcall.lease_ttl are present in the config YAML. If upgrading from older release, no DB migrations required.
